greeting.purpose: The cover greeting in foil script. Sized by container query against the cover leaf.

signature.purpose: The sign-off on the letter, in cranberry script.

headline.purpose: One per sheet. Raised to clamp(2rem, 5.4vw, 3.5rem) on the addressed envelope.

hook.purpose: The plain-words line under the greeting; half of the single h1.

title.purpose: Sub-headings on a sheet and the maker line.

numeral.purpose: The years 1999 and 2026, step numbers, year tags and the wipe sheet.

letter.purpose: Body text of the letter only, capped at 60ch.

control.purpose: Select values, the quiet button, the skip link.

lede.purpose: Opening paragraph of the comparison sheet and the send pitch.

small.purpose: Maker card, notes, checkbox labels, maker links.

label.purpose: Field labels, edition captions, the enclosures label.

shadows.name: paper-shadow
shadows.purpose: Any piece of paper lying on the blotter: envelope, card, sheets, addressed envelope, maker card. Shipped as --paper-shadow.

shadows.name: picture
shadows.purpose: The game and the comparison frame, with a 1px ink outline.

shadows.name: knob
shadows.purpose: The comparison knob, ringed in card white.

shadows.name: comparison-line
shadows.purpose: The 4px leaning line on the comparison.

shadows.name: fold-cover
shadows.purpose: Crease on the cover leaf; inset 0 -16px 20px -16px once the card stacks.

shadows.name: fold-inside
shadows.purpose: Crease on the inside leaf; inset 0 16px 20px -16px once the card stacks.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for every transition and both keyframe animations. Shipped as --ease-out.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: The envelope settling once on arrival. The only arrival animation.

motion.name: strike
motion.value: 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) forwards; from opacity 0, scale(1.9), blur(3px) to opacity 0.92
motion.purpose: The dated postmark struck when the page is sent or the link copied.

motion.name: plate-wipe-cover
motion.purpose: Cranberry year sheet wiping in over the game from the left; artwork changes after 270ms.

motion.name: plate-wipe-leave
motion.purpose: Year sheet wiping off to the right after a 460ms minimum hold and once the game draws the new artwork.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Stamp lift, edition print lift, knob scale, FAQ plus rotation, enclosure arrow drop.

motion.name: tint
motion.purpose: Colour, background and border changes on hover.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All motion removed; a struck postmark stays visible at 0.92 opacity; the artwork changes without the wipe.

breakpoints.name: phone-landscape
breakpoints.value: orientation: landscape and max-height: 520px and pointer: coarse

texture.name: grain
texture.value: SVG fractalNoise, baseFrequency 0.85, 2 octaves, alpha 0.09, 180px tile
texture.purpose: Laid over the flat colour of every paper surface and the blotter. Shipped as --grain. Pictures carry no grain.

focus.purpose: --focus is on-blotter by default (desk and cranberry cover), cranberry on white and silver paper and on the full-screen button, card on the turn-your-phone panel.

fitReserveH.note: Unitless pixel height the page keeps around a fit-to-window game; read by game.js.

stageW.note: Written on the root by game.js; the row under the plate is min(100%, var(--stage-w)).

artwork.note: Visually hidden select owned by the game. The two edition radios and the [data-edition] buttons set its value and dispatch change; the page reflects #game-container[data-artwork].

projectRules: No inline script (Content-Security-Policy); behaviour lives in web/js/page.js.
No invented logos or brand marks.

narrative.overview:
The page is a piece of December post lying open on a desk. A spruce-green blotter is the ground, a silver envelope is slipped under an open card, the card's cranberry cover leaf sits beside its white inside leaf, and the playable game is tipped into that inside leaf like a print held by corner mounts. Everything further down is another piece of paper from the same envelope: a rules slip, a comparison sheet, a letter with a list tucked half under it, the small print, the envelope turned over and addressed, and the maker's card.

Every surface is paper, so every surface carries the same fine grain, square corners and one soft cast shadow, and most pieces lie a fraction of a degree off square. Colour is used the way a two-colour print job uses it: cranberry and black ink on white stock, silver for the envelope and the foil greeting, green only for the desk. Density is that of a printed card, not an app: one large picture, short lines of slab type, and controls set as the blanks on a reply card.

Motion is nearly absent. The envelope settles once when the page arrives, a cranberry sheet with the year wipes across the game when the artwork changes, and a dated postmark is struck when the page is sent on. Nothing animates on scroll.
keyCharacteristics: Green blotter ground; all content sits on separate pieces of paper with a shared grain and cast shadow.
One accent, cranberry, used for the card cover, corner mounts, the chosen print, links and the primary action.
Three type voices: a brush script used twice, a Clarendon slab for everything printed, a grotesque for reading text and labels.
Square corners everywhere; the only circles are the postmark and the knob on the comparison line.
Paper tilts by 2 degrees or less; the game itself is never tilted.
The game is in the first viewport at every size, and a phone held sideways shows nothing else.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: On white and silver paper there are two inks, cranberry and black: every action and link is one or the other. Green belongs to the desk, and silver is an ink only on cranberry.

rules.name: The Lit Ring Rule
rules.body: The focus ring is 2.5px solid with a 3px offset and takes its colour from the surface it sits on: On Blotter on the desk and the cranberry cover, Cranberry on white and silver paper, Card White on the deep-cranberry phone panel.

rules.name: The Brush Twice Rule
rules.body: The script appears in two places: the greeting on the cover and the signature on the letter. It never sets a heading, a button or a caption.

rules.name: The Printed Year Rule
rules.body: 1999 and 2026 are always Besley 900 with tight negative tracking, wherever they appear.

rules.name: The Slab Acts Rule
rules.body: If the reader can press it, open it or choose it, its text is Besley 700. Hanken Grotesk is for sentences and for the small label above a field.

rules.name: The Where It Fell Rule
rules.body: Paper tilts by 2 degrees or less and only whole pieces tilt. The card, the game, the comparison frame and all running text stay square.

rules.name: The Game First Rule
rules.body: At every breakpoint the game is in the first viewport; the cover gives up content before the game gives up space.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: Every piece of paper on the blotter takes the same cast shadow. Height is shown by tilt and overlap, never by a bigger or differently coloured shadow.

rules.name: The Settle Once Rule
rules.body: The only arrival animation is the envelope settling (0.7s, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)). Nothing animates on scroll, and reduced-motion removes every transition and animation while leaving a struck postmark visible.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Paper has no radius. A circle is allowed only where the object is round in the post: a postmark, or a knob.

dos: Do put every new block of content on its own piece of paper: card white or envelope silver with grain, the paper shadow, square corners, and a tilt of 2 degrees or less.
Do keep cranberry as the single accent on paper, for the primary action, links, numerals and marks, and keep green for the desk.
Do set anything pressable in Besley 700 and anything read in Hanken Grotesk; keep the script for the greeting and the signature.
Do set 1999 and 2026 in Besley 900 with negative tracking wherever the years appear.
Do mount pictures of the game with cranberry corner triangles and a 1px ink outline on picture white.
Do point the focus ring at a colour that reads on the surface: On Blotter on green and cranberry, Cranberry on white and silver.
Do keep the game in the first viewport at every size and keep the game hooks listed in the page-to-game contract intact.
Do put all page behaviour in external script files; the Content-Security-Policy forbids inline script.
Do use real project assets for every picture and mark: recovered 1999 sprites, the redrawn characters, the Inventing Fire mark.
donts: Don't round the corners of paper, buttons, fields or prints; circles are for the postmark and the comparison knob.
Don't tilt the card, the game, the comparison frame or running text.
Don't add scroll-triggered animation; the envelope settles once and the rest is still.
Don't give paper a second shadow style to suggest importance; use overlap and tilt.
Don't use green as a button or link colour, or silver as ink anywhere but on cranberry.
Don't let tilted paper widen the page; bands clip horizontally.
Don't draw, generate or approximate a logo or brand mark; use the real asset file or leave it out.
Don't add testimonials, press quotes, play counts or any number that is not in the project's evidence.
Don't rename, remove or restyle away the controls the game script reads.
